title: Factors, Prime Factors, LCM and HCF
seo_title: LCM and HCF – JSS 1 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Find factors, multiples and prime factors of whole numbers; write numbers as products of prime factors; find the LCM and HCF; solve problems. (summary of the NERDC JSS 1 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free JSS 1 maths worksheets on factors and multiples, prime factorisation, the highest common factor (HCF) and lowest common multiple (LCM), and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Prime factors give the HCF and LCM
key_sub: HCF: shared primes. LCM: all primes, highest powers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Write a number as a product of prime factors using a factor tree: 72 = 2³ × 3².
  • HCF: multiply the prime factors common to all the numbers, using the lowest power.
  • LCM: multiply every prime factor that appears, using the highest power.

Examples

Example

HCF and LCM of 36 and 60

36 = 2² × 3², 60 = 2² × 3 × 5

Answer: HCF = 12, LCM = 180

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Including 1 as a prime1 is not a prime number.
Multiplying all factors for the HCFOnly the shared ones.
Using the lowest power for the LCMUse the highest power.

items.q: Which number is a factor of 40?
items.e: 40 ÷ 8 = 5 with no remainder, so 8 is a factor of 40. A factor divides into the number exactly.

items.q: Which number is a factor of 63?
items.e: 63 ÷ 21 = 3 with no remainder, so 21 is a factor of 63. A factor divides into the number exactly.

items.q: Write 72 as a product of prime factors in index form.
items.e: Divide by primes: 2 appears 3 times, 3 appears 2 times. So 72 = 23 × 32.

items.q: Find the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 10 and 16.
items.e: Multiples of 10: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, … The first one that is also a multiple of 16 is 80. (10 × 16 = 160 is a common multiple, but not the lowest.)

items.q: 12 = 22 × 3 and 18 = 2 × 32. Find the HCF of 12 and 18.
items.e: HCF: take each prime in both, with the lower power. LCM: take every prime, with the higher power. The HCF is 6.

items.q: Two school bells ring together at 8:00 a.m. One rings every 11 minutes and the other every 9 minutes. After how many minutes will they next ring together?
items.e: We need the lowest common multiple of 11 and 9: 99 minutes.

items.q: Biscuits come in packets of 10 and drinks come in packs of 7. What is the smallest number of each you can buy so that you have the same number of biscuits and drinks?
items.e: LCM of 10 and 7 = 70.

items.q: Biscuits come in packets of 10 and drinks come in packs of 5. What is the smallest number of each you can buy so that you have the same number of biscuits and drinks?
